parole.significato: Used to form plurals of some Hebrew and Yiddish loanwords, usually ending in -a or -ah.
parole.testo: From the traditional Ashkenazi pronunciation of Hebrew ־וֹת (“-ót”), and its descendant, Yiddish ־ות (-es).

parole.significato: A traditional bread eaten by Ashkenazi Jews, usually braided for the Sabbath and round for a yom tov.
parole.testo: From Hebrew חַלָּה (ḥallá, “loaf”), influenced by Yiddish חלה (khale).

parole.significato: A selection from the books of Nevi'im and Ketuvim of the Tanach, usually corresponding to the week's parashah, publicly…
parole.testo: From Hebrew הַפְטָרָה (haftará), also through Yiddish הפֿטרה (haftore). parole.significato: A circle dance popular in the Balkans, Israel and Yiddish culture worldwide.
parole.testo: From Hebrew הוֹרָה (hóra), Yiddish האָרע (hore), and Romanian horă, from Turkish hora, probably from Greek χορός (chorós, “dance”). Doublet of choir, chorus, and quire.

parole.significato: The person who reads the Haftarah.
parole.testo: From Hebrew מַפְטִיר (maftír), also through Yiddish מפֿטיר (mafter).

parole.significato: The person who performs the circumcision in a Jewish bris.
parole.testo: From Hebrew מוֹהֵל (mohél), but the common pronunciations are borrowed via Yiddish מוהל (moyel).

parole.significato: A type of Ashkenazi Jewish worship song.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hebrew נִגּוּן (nigún) probably through Yiddish ניגון (nigun).

parole.significato: Sidelocks worn by Hasidic and Orthodox male Jews.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hebrew פֵּאוֹת (pe'ót) or Yiddish פּאות (peyes).

parole.significato: Used Saturday night through Sunday (and sometimes later) to express good wishes for the coming week following the Jewis…
parole.testo: From Hebrew שבוע טוב (shavúa tov, “good week”), from Yiddish אַ גוטע וואָך (a gute vokh).

parole.significato: A weeklong period of formal mourning for a close relative.
parole.testo: From Hebrew שִׁבְעָה (shiv'á, “seven”), referring to the number of days that shiva spans. The pronunciation is likely in part from Yiddish שבֿעה (shive).

parole.significato: A very righteous person, especially a Hassidic spiritual leader.
parole.testo: From Hebrew צַדִּיק (tsadík, “righteous person”). Many pronunciations have come under the influence of Yiddish צדיק (tsadek).

parole.significato: A major religious holiday, on which a certain set of rules and prohibitions applies.
parole.testo: From Hebrew יוֹם טוֹב (yom tov). Pronunciation from Yiddish יום־טובֿ (yontev).
